reason: I’ll start building the gas giant by gathering icy planetesimals into a larger core.
expectation: Gravitational focusing may accelerate the growth of an outer planetary core.

alternatives.reason: The later-growing core could lead toward the less gaseous world, but I’ll follow the earlier growth path first.

effect: The icy planetesimals formed a growing rock-and-ice core, so I can follow its growth toward a gas giant.
reaction: The distinction between icy building material and a frozen modern interior was useful.
reason: Gravity around the growing core seems relevant to gathering its gas envelope.
expectation: The core may begin attracting surrounding gas, though I’m unsure how much it will gather at this stage.

alternatives.reason: This could advance the later-growing world, but I’ll finish the first growth path before switching.

effect: The core now holds hydrogen and helium, but its envelope must lose energy before it can gather more gas.
reaction: Cooling as a requirement for gas accumulation is an interesting detail.
reason: Open space may let the envelope radiate energy and contract.
expectation: The envelope will cool and contract, potentially allowing further gas accumulation.

alternatives.reason: The later-growing core remains relevant to the other goal, but I’ll continue the gas-giant path first.

effect: The envelope has cooled and contracted, allowing the disk to replenish its gas.
reaction: The connection between energy loss and continued gas accumulation makes sense.
reason: Combining the envelope with the disk should advance the gas-giant goal.
expectation: The contracting envelope may gather substantially more gas from the disk.

alternatives.reason: The later-growing core serves the other goal, but I’ll continue this path first.

effect: The gas giant is complete, so I’ll turn to the remaining volatile-rich world goal.
reaction: It was useful to see cooling lead to rapid gas accumulation, with the formation model qualified as active research.
reason: The later-growing core and icy outer-disk material appear to start the remaining path.
expectation: The core will gather rock and ice, potentially becoming a volatile-rich world with less gas.

effect: The late core has gathered rock and volatiles while less gas remains, advancing the remaining goal.
reaction: The timing contrast with the gas giant is clear.
reason: The dispersing disk should show how limited gas availability affects the late core.
expectation: The core will become a volatile-rich world with a smaller gas envelope, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The gas giant could interact with icy planetesimals, but the late core is more directly relevant to the remaining goal.

effect: The late core became an ice-giant-like world with a modest gas envelope, completing the remaining goal and clarifying the role of disk depletion.
reaction: The contrast with the gas giant was clear, especially the reminder that its interior need not be frozen ice.

mostWorthwhile.text: Cooling the gas envelope was most worthwhile: it explained why losing energy allows a core to accumulate more gas.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the initial rock-and-ice core felt comparatively routine, though it set up the later contrast.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected envelope cooling to be necessary for continued gas accumulation.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the combinations followed the stated physical processes and goals.

continue.text: Yes. The contrast between early and late core growth made me curious how the resulting worlds might affect their surroundings.
